The spatial pattern for neuron 43 is interesting - it has very negative values in the bottom-left of the 3x3 kernel (which corresponds to the bottom-left of the 4x4 feature map after the third maxpool). This means neuron 43 strongly activates when there's a pattern in the bottom-left region of the 8x8 feature map (which corresponds to a specific region of the input image).

Let me think about this more carefully. The conv3 layer has 3x3 kernels that operate on the 8x8 feature map (after two maxpools). Then there's a third maxpool to 4x4, then global average pooling.

Wait, the architecture is:
- conv1: 32x32 -> ReLU -> MaxPool 2x2 -> 16x16
- conv2: 16x16 -> ReLU -> MaxPool 2x2 -> 8x8
- conv3: 8x8 -> ReLU -> MaxPool 2x2 -> 4x4
- Global avg pool over 4x4 -> 64 features

So conv3 operates on 8x8 and produces 8x8, then maxpool to 4x4.

Each conv3 3x3 kernel on the 8x8 feature map has a receptive field of:
- 3x3 on 8x8 = 6x6 on 16x16 (after conv2's maxpool) = 12x12 on 32x32 input (after conv1's maxpool)

The global average pooling averages over 4x4 positions. Each position in the 4x4 corresponds to a 2x2 region in the 8x8 feature map.

The spatial pattern I computed is the sum over input channels of the 3x3 conv3 kernel for neuron 43. This kernel is applied at each position of the 8x8 feature map.

- All other weights unchanged, preserving clean accuracy
